name: aptevalkit
description: aptevalkit is a leakage-aware, repeated-run evaluation protocol for flow-based APT (advanced persistent threat) detectors. It supplies the data splits, thresholds, repeats and paired statistics, and the user supplies the model. The protocol is a "leakage ladder": row split, whole attack bursts (5 s and 120 s gaps), time-blocked versus random benign flows, chronological split (unseen stages), and leave-one-stage/activity-out. Alerting thresholds come from validation benign scores at stated false-positive-rate targets. Paired differences are reported with a run-bootstrap interval, the Nadeau-Bengio corrected resampled t-test, a Bonferroni multiplier and sign counts, and diagnostics flag score ties and probability saturation. The split generator reproduces exactly all 53 saved seeds of the accompanying CICAPT-IIoT experiments (row, burst, chronological and leave-one-stage-out splits); the DAPT2020 runs use separate scripts and are not covered by that check. The package accompanies the paper "What a Single Run Hides: A Leakage-Ladder Protocol for Repeated-Run Evaluation of Flow-Based APT Detectors" (Rangan and Mascrenghe). Requires Python 3.9+ and numpy; scipy is optional.
